title: Yield and Cryoresistance of Primordial Germ Cells Differ Among Ten Rare Chicken Breeds: Implications for Poultry Gene Banking
content: Conserving the rare and indigenous breeds of domesticated birds accumulated by generations of breeders is an essential task of modern agricultural science. The approach used for mammals, in which germ cells and embryos are cryopreserved for gene banks, cannot be applied to birds because of their unique reproductive system. A solution lies in acquiring and cryopreserving avian primordial germ cells (PGCs), which would help conserve the distinct genotypes of uncommon and endangered breeds and species of domestic and wild birds. In this study, PGCs were obtained from embryos of ten non-industrial chicken breeds maintained in a genetic collection, cultivated in vitro, cryopreserved and thawed; in total, 295 cell culture samples were analysed. The concentration of cells produced in culture and their viability after cryopreservation were assessed separately for each breed. A correlation coefficient of 0.46 was found between PGC concentration in the sample and the productive specialisation of the breed, and a coefficient of 0.51 between the level of egg production and PGC cryoresistance. The highest coefficient, 0.79, was observed between PGC concentration in culture and survival after cryopreservation, indicating that cryobanking of low-yielding ornamental and game breeds requires more embryos and extended cultivation before freezing.
